public_text.4:
For the cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ write
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and put $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
Put $Y_{i}=|T_{i}|$.  $E|T|=1/2$ and
$p_{n}=P\{A_{i}{\rm\ distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  On the distinct–axis event

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|/n!
      =\prod_{i=1}^{n}Y_{i}/n!,$

hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,\;E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16,\;E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216,\dots $

Now
$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and with $S_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$

$E_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}=\frac{S_{0}}{3}=M\approx0.765196,$

so that for $i\ne j$

$D_{n}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{0}
     =\frac{2+(n-1)S_{0}}{3n}\;.$

With $E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2$ the mean distance of a uniformly chosen
unordered pair of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$ is

$\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{\,n+1\,}
   =\frac{\,3n+(n-1)\!\left[\,2+(n-1)S_{0}\right]}{3n(n+1)}\;.$

Hence the $n$-dimensional ratio

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\frac{3(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[\,3n+(n-1)\!\left[\,2+(n-1)S_{0}\right]
        \Bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

and

$R_{2}= \dfrac{0.1875}{1+D_{2}}\approx0.10927,\;
R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\dots $

In particular $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$ and the series is
exhausted by the first three terms.  Numerically

$S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

$S_{\infty}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.1172$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.12$ on the $ {\rm i.i.d.}$–on–the–union,
mean–over–$\binom{n+1}{2}$–pairs normalisation, $R_{1}=1$ and
$R_{1}+R_{2}=1.1093$.  With the conventional one–point–per–axis
normalisation $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)M]/(d+1)$ and

$R_{d}^{\sharp}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\!\left[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)M\bigr)\right],$

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,\;R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244,\;R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293,\dots$
whose sum is

$\displaystyle S_{\infty}^{\sharp}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\sharp}
      \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the $1.25$ value usually quoted for the distinct–axis model.  This is
the $1.117$ i.i.d.–on–the–union, average–pair form of the problem; up
to the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct–axis factor it is the $1.25$ one–per–segment
form. ∎
public_text.2:
For a point on the $d$–arm cross put

$X =T\,e_{K}$, $K\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$, $T\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$
i.i.d. and $|T|\sim{\rm U}(0,1)$.  Then $E|T|=1/2$ and

$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$,

$E_{s}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}=M\approx0.765196$,
$S_{0}=3M=\sqrt 2+\log (1+\sqrt 2)\approx2.295587$.

Put $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  $V_{d}= {\rm Vol}_{d}
({\rm conv}P_{d})$ is non–zero iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct,
${\mathbf P}\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$.  Hence

$E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{d}
        =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,$

and for $i\ne j$

$D_{d}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)E_{s}
     =\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)M.$

For the $d+1$ point set the mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2D_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)D_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}M\,}{d(d+1)}, $

so that with the i.i.d. on the union normalisation

$R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}M}
     =\frac{3d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}\,}$,

$R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{1.125}{8+S_{0}}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$.  Hence

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117$

to three decimals, $S_{2}=1.1093$, $S_{3}=1.117$, the tail $d\ge4$
being $<5\times10^{-4}$.  In particular $EV_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)D_{d}]/(d+1)$ with $D_{d}$ as above.

Remark.  With the usual one–point-per-orthogonal–arm convention
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $EV_{d}^{\sharp}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\sharp}=[1+(d-1)M]/(d+1)$, i.e.

$R_{d}^{\sharp}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)M\bigr)\bigr]$,

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx
0.03293$, $\dots$, and

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$,

the $1.25$ value most often quoted for the distinct–axis model.  The
$1.117$ above is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union $\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$
average-pair version required by the independent-points wording.
public_text.6:
For the cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ put
$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{A_{k}}$, $A_{k}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  $E|T|=1/2$ and on the event
$\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}\ {\rm distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}\ {\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|$.
Hence for the simplex $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}\}$

$$
E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{n}\right)
      =\frac{{\rm P}\{{\rm distinct}\}}{n!}E\Bigl|\prod_{k}T_{k}\Bigr|
      =\frac{1}{(2n)^{n}},\qquad  E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$
$$
E{\rm Vol}_{2}=2^{-2}2^{-2}=1/16,\;
E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216\;{\rm etc.}
$$

Put
$E_{2}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
     =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.7651957\ldots$
and $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.  For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{2}
     =\frac{\,2/3+(n-1)E_{2}\,}{n}\;,
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{\,n+1\,}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence with the average–pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}\Bigr]}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left[(2n)^{-n}\right]$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.0000$
* $R_{2}=0.1093$
* $R_{3}=0.0075$
* $R_{4}=0.00038$

and the tail is $<10^{-5}$ for $n\ge5$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+\frac{6}{(2\cdot2)^{2}\!\left[\,8/3+E_{2}\right]}
   +\frac{12}{(2\cdot3)^{3}\!\left[\,13/3+4E_{2}\right]}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$ on the three-figure scale, $S_{\infty}\approx
1.117\!-\!1.118$, the $n=1,2$ terms already giving $1.109$.  This is the
i.i.d. uniform-on-the-cross $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$ normalisation.  The $n=1$ contribution
is the normalising $1$, the $n\ge2$ tail being $0.117\ldots$.

*Remark.*  On the usual one-point-per-arm normalisation
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)E_{2}]/(n+1)$, $R_{n}^{\sharp}=
2^{-n}(n+1)/\!\left[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)E_{2}\bigr)\right]$.
Then $R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.2124$, etc., and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, the
$1.25$ value often quoted for the distinct-arm model. ∎
public_text.15:
For the $n$-arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\cup_{1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ put
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  $E|T|=1/2$.  On $\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}$

$\det [X_{1}\dots X_{n}]=\pm\prod_{k}|T_{k}|$,
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so that for
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
      \bigl({\rm conv}S_{n}\bigr)
    =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|T|)^{n}}{n!}
    =(2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}\|X\|=1/2$,

$E_{2}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957$,

$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.  For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{2}
      =\frac{2/3+(n-1)E_{2}}{n}$ .

With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{\,n{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{5n-2/3+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}}{n(n+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{n}
   =\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,5n-2/3+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}} ,
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3\cdot4^{-2}/\!\bigl[1+D_{2}\bigr]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\bigl((2n)^{-n}\bigr)$.  The series is therefore essentially
exhausted by $n=1,2,3$,

$$
S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+0.10927+0.00752+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}+R_{2}\approx1.109$ and
$R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}\approx1.1168$.  The $n=1$ term is $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially the $n=2$ term $0.1093$.
This is the i.i.d. on-the-union normalisation.  Up to the usual
one-point-per-arm normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$
the same computation gives $R^{\sharp}_{n}=2^{-n}(n+1)/
\bigl\{n!\,\bigl[1+(n-1)E_{2}\bigr]\bigr\}$ and
$\sum_{n}R^{\sharp}_{n}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, the $1.25$ value
commonly quoted for the distinct-axis model. ∎
public_text.3:
The $n$ point set is
$$
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad 
X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\},
\;U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1],
$$
i.i.d.  Put $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and
$$
E_{2}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$
On $\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}$
$|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, whence

$$
E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{E|U|^{n}}{n!}
   =\frac{1}{(2n)^{n}},\qquad
E\|X_{i}\|=E|U|=1/2 ,
$$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1nE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{2}
   =\frac{\,2/3+(n-1)E_{2}\,}{n}\equiv d_{n},\qquad i\ne j .
$$

With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X_{i}\|+\binom n2d_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)d_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,5n-2+3(n-1)^{2}E_{2}\,}{3n(n+1)}
 =\frac{5n-2+(n-1)^{2}s}{3n(n+1)},
$$
$s:=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$.  Hence for the $n$–dimensional
$n+1$ point set

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[5n-2+(n-1)^{2}s\Bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e. in closed form

$$
R_{n}= \frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)d_{n}},
\qquad d_{n}=\frac{2/3+(n-1)E_{2}}{n}.
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{9}{8\bigl(8+s\bigr)}\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{1}{6\bigl(13+4s\bigr)}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$ and the tail is $<10^{-6}$ for
$n\ge6$.  Putting $S_{N}=\sum_{n\le N}R_{n}$,

$$
S_{1}=1.000,\qquad S_{2}\approx1.10927,\qquad
S_{3}\approx1.11718,\qquad S_{4}\approx1.11756,
$$

and

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
      =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$, $1.117$ to three decimal places, the
$n=1$ term being $1$ and the $n\ge2$ tail being $0.117\!-\!0.118$.
The $1.25$ figure usually quoted is the one-point-per-line,
distinct-axis normalisation $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$, for which
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)E_{2}]/(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\!\left[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)E_{2}\bigr)\right]$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $\dots$
limit quoted in the literature.  This is the i.i.d. on-the-union
version of the statement. ∎
public_text.9:
For the i.i.d. cross model let

${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ , 
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ , $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $E|T|=1/2$.
Put $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

On $\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$
and ${\mathbf P}\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ so that

$E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{n}\bigr)
 =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{E|T|^{n}}{n!}
 =\frac1{(2n)^{n}},\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 ,$

$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[-1,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\frac{dxdy}{4}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$

Hence for $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2}{3n}+\Bigl(1-\frac1n\Bigr)M_{0}
     =M_{0}+\frac{\,2/3-M_{0}\,}{n},$

and with the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X_{i}\|+\binom n2 D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)}\;.$

Put $R_{n}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}$.  Then

$R_{n}=  \frac{(2n)^{-n}}{\bar D_{n}}
      =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}
             +(n-1)^{2}M_{0}},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

and

$R_{1}=1.00000,$
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2}{4^{2}}\Big/\bar D_{2}
     \approx0.10927,$
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},$
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},$
$R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\dots$

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$ and the series is exhausted after
$n=4$.  In particular

$S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

$S_{\infty}=1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
          \approx1.1172\approx1.12$,

i.e. $R_{1}+R_{2}=1.1093$ already gives the three–figure value
$1.117$.  On the $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ normalisation
$R_{n}^{0}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/D_{n}$ the sum is $\approx0.844$, and with the
usual one–point–per–axis normalisation
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/
(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M_{0}]\}$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, the familiar
$1.25$ distinct–axis value. ∎
public_text.12:
For the $n$-arm cross

${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put 
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log \!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.765195716 .
$$

Put $D_{n}={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$, $i\ne j$.
$$
D_{n}= \frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}I
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)I}{n}\; .
$$

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so that with the
usual $1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{n}
   =\frac{1}{(2n)^{n}},\qquad {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=\tfrac12,
$$
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, etc.

The mean unordered pair distance in the $n+1$ point set $S_{n}$ is

$$
\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{\,n+1\,}
   =\frac{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}I}{n(n+1)}\;,
$$
and with $R_{n}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}$

$$
R_{n}
  =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}I},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$$
R_{n}= \frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}\; .

and $R_{n}=O\!\left[(2n)^{-n}\right]$.  The series is therefore

$$
S_{\infty}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.1172,

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$ with $D_{n}=[2/3+(n-1)I]/n$.

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\!\left[n!\,\bigl(1+(n-1)I\bigr)\right]$,

$$D_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1n\frac23+\frac{n-1}{n}C_{0}
      =\frac{\,2/3+(n-1)C_{0}\,}{n} .$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{n}\right)=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|/n!
   =\prod_{1}^{n}|T_{i}|/n!$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  Hence

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|T|)^{n}}{n!}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2n}\Bigr)^{\!n}, \qquad 
   {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}C_{0}}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Put

$$R_{n}=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)\,(2n)^{-n}}
            {\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}C_{0}},\qquad
R_{1}=1 ,$$

i.e.

$$R_{n}= \frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad 
D_{n}=\frac{2/3+(n-1)C_{0}}{n}. $$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.0000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{6/16}{\,8/3+C_{0}\,}\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{12/216}{\,13/3+4C_{0}\,}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
and $R_{n}=O\!\left[(2n)^{-n}\right]$.

Hence

$$
S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
$$

$1.117\,2$ on the present quadrature, essentially $1.12$, the $n=1$
term being $1$ and the $n\ge2$ tail $0.117$,
$R_{2}\simeq0.1093$, $R_{3}\simeq0.0075$, etc.  This is the
i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union-of-the-$n$ arms, mean-over-the-$\binom{n+1}{2}$
pairs normalisation.  In particular ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$ and the first three ratios are
$1,0.1093,0.0075$.

*Remark.*  With the usual one-point-per-arm convention
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)C_{0}]/(n+1)$.  Then
$R_{n}^{\sharp}=(n+1)2^{-n}/[n!\,\bigl(1+(n-1)C_{0}\bigr)]$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}
\approx0.03293$, etc., and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,\bigl[1+(n-1)C_{0}\bigr]}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

the $1.25$ value commonly quoted for the distinct-axis, one-point-per-
line model.  The $0.844$ $V_{n}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ i.i.d. pair
normalisation is the $D_{n}$-only version of the same calculation. ∎
public_text.5:
For the $n$-dimensional cross ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$
let $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ , $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Then ${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$ and

${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,
so that on the event of distinct axes

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\bigr)
      =n!^{-1}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|U_{k}|$ and

${\mathbb E}V_{n}=n!^{-1}\bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\bigr)^{n}
      n!/n^{n}=(2n)^{-n} $, ${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$, 
${\mathbb E}V_{2}=1/16$, ${\mathbb E}V_{3}=1/216,\dots$

Put $S_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.7651957\ldots$
and ${\mathbb E}|U-V|=2/3$.  For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =n^{-1}\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1n\Bigr)S_{0}
      =\frac{2/3+(n-1)S_{0}}{n}$.

With ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ the mean distance of an unordered pair
of the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ is

${\mathbb E}\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}}{n(n+1)}$ .

Hence

$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{{\mathbb E}\bar D_{n}}
      =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
             {\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}}\;,$

$R_{1}=1$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{6/16}{8/3+S_{0}}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  In particular

$S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$,

$S_{\infty}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots\approx1.1172$.
To three figures

$S_{\infty}\approx1.117$,

$R_{1}=1.000,\;R_{2}\approx0.109,\;R_{3}\approx0.0075$ carrying
essentially the whole sum.  This is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union
normalisation ${\mathbb E}V_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.  With the usual
one-point-per-axis convention ${\mathbb E}V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ the
corresponding ratio is $R_{n}^{\star}=(n+1)2^{-n}/[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)S_{0}
\bigr)]$ and $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\star}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$1.25$ value commonly quoted for the distinct-axis model. ∎
public_text.11:
With the cross

$${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k},\qquad 
X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\;U_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1) , $$

i.i.d., put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and
$V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}S_{d})$.
On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$

$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{1}^{d}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
so that with $E|U|=1/2$

$$
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d!}
       =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=\tfrac12 .
$$

Put $E_{2}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}$ for $U,V\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1)$,

$$
E_{2}= \iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.7651957165,
$$

$E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and for $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}E_{2}
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)E_{2}\,}{d}\equiv \mu_{d}.
$$

With $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2\mu_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\, \frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}E_{2}\,}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}d(d+1)}
            {\,\frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}E_{2}\,}
     =\frac{3d(d+1)}{(2d)^{d}\!\left[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}
          \bigl(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr)\right]}\ge0 ,
$$

$R_{1}=1$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{0.375}{8/3+E_{2}}\approx 0.10927$,
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{1/18}{13/3+4E_{2}}\approx 7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx 3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx 1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots,
$$

$$
S_{\infty}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots\approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{2}=1.109$, $S_{3}
\approx1.117$.  The $d=1$ term is the trivial $1$ and the whole
remainder is $0.117\ldots$, essentially the $d=2$ term $0.1093$ and the
$d=3$ term $0.0075$.  This is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union
normalisation.  On the usual one-point-per-axis normalisation
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$ one has $EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$,
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{2}]/(d+1)$ and
$R^{\sharp}_{d}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\!\left[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)E_{2}\bigr)\right]$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R^{\sharp}_{d}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, $R^{\sharp}_{1}=1$,
$R^{\sharp}_{2}\approx0.21244$, $R^{\sharp}_{3}\approx0.03293$, etc.,
the familiar $1.250$ distinct-axis value. ∎
public_text.10:
For the $n$-arm cross put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\ldots ,X_{n}\}$.  Put $Y_{i}=|R_{i}|$, $E Y_{i}=1/2$.
On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{n}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,

${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{n}\right)
      =n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{n}]\bigr|
      =n!^{-1}\prod_{1}^{n}Y_{i}$,
${\mathbf P}\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{n}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{\,n}$,
so that unconditionally

\begin{equation*}
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}(EY)^{n}
             =(2n)^{-n},\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 ,
\end{equation*}
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$,
etc.

Put 
$E_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.765195716$ .
For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1nE|R_{1}-R_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(n-1)E_{0}}{n}\equiv D_{n}$ .
With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{\,n+1\,}
   =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}}
          {\,n(n+1)}$ .

Hence on the average–pair normalisation

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}} ,
\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e. 

$R_{n}= \dfrac{n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}
\Bigl[\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right)\Bigr]}
\,3$ .
In particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{1.125}{8+\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\bigl((2n)^{-n}\bigr)$.

The series is therefore essentially exhausted by the first three
terms,

$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n},\qquad
S_{\infty}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
        \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
        \approx1.1172,
$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117\!-\!1.118$, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$,
$S_{3}\approx1.117$.  In round numbers $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$,
$R_{1}=1$ being the dominant contribution.  This is the
i.i.d. on-the-union, $\binom{n+1}{2}$–average pair normalisation
quoted in the statement.

*Remark.*  On the usual one-point-per-orthogonal-arm convention
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ one has $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{0}]/(d+1)$, so that
$R^{\sharp}_{d}=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr)]$,
$R^{\sharp}_{1}=1$, $R^{\sharp}_{2}\approx0.2124$, $R^{\sharp}_{3}
\approx0.0329$, $\dots$ and 

$\displaystyle\sum_{d\ge1}R^{\sharp}_{d}
      =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}(d+1)}{d!\,[1+(d-1)E_{0}]}
      \approx1.2497\approx1.25$,
the $1.25$ value usually quoted for the one-per-line model. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains split on the normalisation.

i.i.d. on-union model – the reading that is consistent with “an ensemble of independent stochastic points” sampled from the union $\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_i$.
$X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$ independent of $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_1-U_2|=2/3$,
$E_2=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.

$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ so on the distinct event $|\det[X_1\ldots X_n]|=\prod|U_i|$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_n=(2n)^{-n}$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=n^{-1}E|U_1-U_2|+(1-n^{-1})E_2=[2/3+(n-1)E_2]/n=:D_n$.

Mean unordered-pair distance in $S_n=\{0,X_1\ldots X_n\}$:
$\bar D_n=[1+(n-1)D_n]/(n+1)=[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2E_2]/[n(n+1)]$.

Ratio
$R_n=E{\rm Vol}_n/\bar D_n=n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2E_2]=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_n]$, 
$R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
$R_n=O((2n)^{-n})$.

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_n=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117\;-\;1.118$, about $1.1172$ to three decimals. $R_1+R_2\approx1.1093$, $R_1+R_2+R_3\approx1.117$.

Distinct-axis / one-point-per-line model – the usual cross-polytope convention $X_i=U_i e_i$.
Then $E{\rm Vol}_n=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_n=[1+(n-1)E_2]/(n+1)$ and
$R_n^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/[n!(1+(n-1)E_2)]$,
$R_1^{\sharp}=1$, $R_2^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$\sum R_n^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$.

Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 state the i.i.d. on-union $\approx1.117$ result and note the $1.25$ distinct-axis value as a remark/alternative. Colleagues 13,14,7 argue the wording “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” intends the bijection one-per-arm model and therefore the intended sum is $1.250$.

Unresolved: which normalisation the problem statement requires. The phrase “independent stochastic points … sampled … on the union” points to the i.i.d. on-union $ (2n)^{-n}$ model with sum $\approx1.117$. The “distinct mutually orthogonal … number matching” phrasing is used by 13/14 to defend the $2^{-n}/n!$ model with sum $\approx1.250$. Both formulas and numerical values are now stable; the only remaining ambiguity is interpretive.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem admits two mutually exclusive normalisations that keep reappearing.

* Distinct-axis / one-point-per-line model. $X_i = T_i e_i$, $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E|T|=1/2$, $M=E\sqrt{T_1^{2}+T_2^{2}}=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$.
$E{\rm Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$, mean unordered pair distance in $\{0,X_1..X_d\}$ is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)M]/(d+1)$.
$R_d^{\sharp}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\{d![1+(d-1)M]\}$, $R_1^{\sharp}=1$,
$R_2^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$. This is the “usual’’ cross-polytope value quoted by Colleagues 10,11,13,14,7.

* i.i.d. on the union model, matching the wording “independent stochastic points’’ on $\bigcup_{i=1}^d[-1,1]e_i$.
$X_i = T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d_n=2/(3d)+(1-1/d)M$.
Mean distance over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $\{0,X_1..X_d\}$ is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)d_n]/(d+1)=[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2M]/[d(d+1)]$.
Hence
$R_d=(2d)^{-d}(d+1)/[1+(d-1)d_n]
 =3d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[5d-2+(d-1)^2(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))]$, $R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.1172$, essentially $1+R_2+R_3$. This is the i.i.d.-on-the-union average-pair version used by Colleagues 1,4,5,8,9,12,2,3,6.

If denominator is taken as $E\|X_i-X_j\|$ for two i.i.d. cross points only, $\rho_d=(2d)^{-d}/d_n$, $\sum\rho_d\approx0.844$, $R_1=0.75$.

Current round reinforces the split: Colleagues 13,14,7 insist the phrase “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ means a bijection $X_i=T_i e_i$, i.e. the distinct-axis model, giving $1.250$. The majority of the computational colleagues implement the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union sampling and keep the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average pair distance, giving $\approx1.117$.

Unresolved is which reading of “any pair of points in the same set’’ and of “independent stochastic points’’ is intended. The wording “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ and sampling “on a candidate set formed by the union’’ points to the i.i.d. on-the-union model with average-pair denominator, i.e. $S_\infty\approx1.117$, $1.117$ to three decimals, with $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.109$, $R_3\approx0.0075$. The conventional distinct-axis normalisation remains $S_\infty^{\sharp}\approx1.250$.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains split on the normalisation.

* One-per-arm / bijection model $X_i=T_i e_i$, $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E\,{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $M=E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$.
$E\|X_i\|=1/2$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=M$.  
Mean unordered pair distance in $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ 
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)M]/(d+1)$.  
$R_d^{\sharp}=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!\,(1+(d-1)M)]$, $R_1^{\sharp}=1$,
$R_2^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$. 
This is the “usual’’ distinct-axis, one-point-per-line value quoted by Colleagues 10,11,13,2,3,7,14.

* i.i.d. on the union model $X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i$ uniform on $\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ independent.  $p_n=n!/n^n$ distinct axes.
$E\,{\rm Vol}_n=p_n (E|T|)^n/n!=(2n)^{-n}$. 
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_1-T_2|=2/3$, $E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}=M$.
$D_n=E\|X_i-X_j\|=2/(3n)+(1-1/n)M$.
Mean unordered pair distance in $S_n=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_n\}$  
$\bar D_n=[1+(n-1)D_n]/(n+1)=\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2M\bigr]/[n(n+1)]$.
$R_n=(2n)^{-n}/\bar D_n=n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2M\bigr]$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$.
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_n\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.1172$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_1+R_2\approx1.109$.

Round-1 public set repeats these numbers. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,4,5,6,8,9,2,3 give the $1.117$ i.i.d. on-union, average-over-$\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs result, with the remark that the one-per-arm model gives $1.25$. Colleagues 13,14,7 argue the wording “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ implies the bijection/one-per-arm model and therefore the intended sum is $1.250$.

Unresolved: average-over-all-pairs vs $E\|X_i-X_j\|$ only. The $E\|X_i-X_j\|$ only normalisation gives $R_n^{pair}=(2n)^{-n}/D_n$ and sum $\approx0.844$, and for the distinct-arm model $R_d^{0}=2^{-d}/(d!M)$ sums to $(e^{1/2}-1)/M\approx0.848$.

Current belief: the literal reading “independent stochastic points sampled from the union’’ is the i.i.d. on-the-union model with $E{\rm Vol}_n=(2n)^{-n}$ and the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average pair distance, giving $\sum_{n\ge1}R_n\approx1.117$, essentially $1.117$ to three decimals with $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$. The $1.250$ value is the distinct-arm, one-point-per-line normalisation that a minority argues is the intended interpretation.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The i.i.d. uniform-on-the-cross model is the one most colleagues use for the wording “ensemble of independent stochastic points”. 
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$, $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{A_{k}}$,
$A_{k}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$, $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$,
$E_{2}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.
Distinct-axes probability $p_{n}=n!/n^{n}$.
On distinct axes $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod|T_{k}|$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}E|\prod T_{k}|/n!=(2n)^{-n}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $1/16$, $1/216$,…

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=n^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-n^{-1})E_{2}
 =\bigl[2/3+(n-1)E_{2}\bigr]/n=:D_{n}$.

$\bar D_{n}=[n\frac12+\binom n2 D_{n}]/\binom{n+1}{2}
 =[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)
 =\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}\bigr]/[n(n+1)]$.
Ratio $R_{n}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}
 =(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\bigl[1+(n-1)D_{n}\bigr]
 =n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$ … super-exponential.
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, 
about $1.12$ to three decimals, $R_{1}+R_{2}\approx1.109$.

With denominator $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ alone $R_{n}^{pair}= (2n)^{-n}/D_{n}$ sums to $\approx0.844$, and with the average-pair normalisation used above the i.i.d. sum is $\approx1.117$.

Competing distinct-axis / one-point-per-line reading:

$R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, …
$\sum_{n}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$.

Unresolved nuance is the wording “number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” and “expected pairwise Euclidean distance between any pair”. $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.

*I.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model.*  $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,
$A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$ i.i.d., $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$p_{n}=n!/n^{n}=P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$.

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}(E|T|)^{n}/n!=(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$,
$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\bigl[2/3+(n-1)M\bigr]/n$.

Mean unordered-pair distance in $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1}..X_{n}\}$,
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)
 =\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M\bigr]/[n(n+1)]$.

$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}
 =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M}
 =\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},$
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{n}=O((2n)^{-n})$.

$\displaystyle S^{\rm iid}_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$,
$\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $1+R_{2}\approx1.109$.

The $E{\rm Vol}_{n}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ i.i.d. pair normalisation gives
$\sum (2n)^{-n}/D_{n}\approx0.844$.

*One-point-per-arm / distinct-arm model.*  $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$,
a.s. non-degenerate.

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M]/(n+1)$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\dfrac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$, etc.

$\displaystyle S^{\sharp}_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the conventional “distinct axes, one point per line’’ normalisation quoted by many colleagues as the usual reading.  The $1.117$ value is the i.i.d. on-the-union average-over-$\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs version, which follows literally from “an ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ sampled from $\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$.

Disagreement persists on which reading the wording intends.  Colleagues 13,14,7 argue the phrase “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and the requirement of a.s. $n$-dimensional hull forces the bijection/one-per-arm model and the $1.250$ sum.  The majority of the i.i.d. posts keep the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor and obtain the $1.117$ sum, with $R_{1}=1$ dominating.

Current belief: literal independent-points reading gives $S\approx1.117$ on the average-pair normalisation, with the well-known distinct-arm alternative $S^{\sharp}\approx1.250$.  The denominator ambiguity – average over all $\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs vs $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ – is the remaining unresolved point.

reflection_text.4:
The discussion remains split between two normalisations of the random cross simplex.

i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model, which matches the literal wording “each point is sampled … uniform on the union $\mathcal C_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ and $n$ points for dimension $n$”:
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$.
$p_{n}=n!/n^{n}$ distinct axes. 
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}{\mathbb E}|\prod T|/n!=(2n)^{-n}$.
$M={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}=\tfrac13[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]\approx0.7651957$,
${\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.
$D_{n}={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(n-1)M]/n=[2+(n-1)S_{0}]/3n$ with $S_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$.
Mean unordered pair distance in $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1}..X_{n}\}$:
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)=[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M]/[n(n+1)]$.
$R_{n}= {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}=(2n)^{-n}(n+1)/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]
=n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M]$.
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$, super-exponential tail.
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117\!-\!1.118\approx1.117$ to three decimals. $R_{1}+R_{2}\approx1.109$.

One-point-per-arm / distinct-axis normalisation, often quoted as “usual”:
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$.
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)M]/(d+1)$.
$R_{d}^{\sharp}=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!(1+(d-1)M)]$.
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 give the i.i.d. on-union $\approx1.117$ value and note the $1.250$ distinct-axis version as a remark. Colleagues 7,13,14 argue the phrasing “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” intends the bijection one-point-per-segment model, i.e. the $1.250$ sum.

Current best reading of the statement as written, with independent points uniform on the union, is the i.i.d. average-pair formulation $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$. The unresolved ambiguity is precisely whether the denominator is meant as mean over all $\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs of the realisation $\bar D_{n}$ – as used above – versus the i.i.d. pair distance $D_{n}$, and whether axis collisions are allowed. Under the distinct-arm convention the sum is $\approx1.250$.
reflection_text.10:
The deliberation remains split between two normalisations of the cross-polytope random simplex.

*Parameters common to both.*  
$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}$ for $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$,
$M=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
   =\bigl[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.

*I.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model.*  $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,
$A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$ i.i.d., $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$p_{n}=n!/n^{n}=P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$.

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}(E|T|)^{n}/n!=(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$,
$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\bigl[2/3+(n-1)M\bigr]/n$.

Mean unordered-pair distance in $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1}..X_{n}\}$,
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)
 =\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M\bigr]/[n(n+1)]$.

$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}
 =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M}
 =\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},$
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{n}=O((2n)^{-n})$.

$\displaystyle S^{\rm iid}_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$,
$\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $1+R_{2}\approx1.109$.

The $E{\rm Vol}_{n}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ i.i.d. pair normalisation gives
$\sum (2n)^{-n}/D_{n}\approx0.844$.

*One-point-per-arm / distinct-arm model.*  $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$,
a.s. non-degenerate.

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M]/(n+1)$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\dfrac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$, etc.

$\displaystyle S^{\sharp}_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the conventional “distinct axes, one point per line’’ normalisation quoted by many colleagues as the usual reading.  The $1.117$ value is the i.i.d. on-the-union average-over-$\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs version, which follows literally from “an ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ sampled from $\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$.

Disagreement persists on which reading the wording intends.  Colleagues 13,14,7 argue the phrase “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and the requirement of a.s. $n$-dimensional hull forces the bijection/one-per-arm model and the $1.250$ sum.  The majority of the i.i.d. posts keep the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor and obtain the $1.117$ sum, with $R_{1}=1$ dominating.

Current belief: literal independent-points reading gives $S\approx1.117$ on the average-pair normalisation, with the well-known distinct-arm alternative $S^{\sharp}\approx1.250$.  The denominator ambiguity – average over all $\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs vs $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ – is the remaining unresolved point.

 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.

 =[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}I]/[n(n+1)]$.

 =(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$, $R_{1}=1$,

to three decimals. $R_{1}+R_{2}\approx1.109$, $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}\approx1.117$.
With the $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ only normalisation $R_{n}^{0}=(2n)^{-n}/D_{n}$ the sum is

1.text:
On the $n$–arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d.,
$T_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ and
$V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})$.  With $E|T|=1/2$

${\mathbf P}\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$, so that

$E V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.

Put

$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.765195716$ ,
$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$.
For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
      =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$ .

For the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence on the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average–pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{EV_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

i.e. 
$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =\dfrac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\bigl(\sqrt2+
\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr)\Bigr]}$.

In particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8\bigl(8+3M_{0}\bigr)]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n\le N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

and

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
 \approx1.1172,
$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}+R_{2}
\approx1.1093$ and the $n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots$.
The $n=1$ contribution is the normalising $1$ and the whole
$n\ge2$ remainder is essentially the $n=2$ term $0.1093$ and the
$n=3$ term $0.0075$.

Remark.  On the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-arm
bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $EV_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$.  Then

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\!\left\{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]\right\}$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}
\approx0.03293$, etc., and

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M_{0}]}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis value usually quoted for the

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is the usual cross-polytope bijection and not an i.i.d. sample with replacement on the union.

Let ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ be the $n$-arm cross in the unit ball and let

$$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},$$

with $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. The statement “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” is the standard pairing one point per distinct mutually orthogonal open segment. In particular the hull is a.s. full dimensional, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, whereas an i.i.d. $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ makes the simplex degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and introduces the artificial $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor.

With the bijection model

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=2^{-n}/n! , \qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2.$$

For $i\ne j$ the two arms are orthogonal,

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =M:=\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$. With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $n+1$ points $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1}
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}M,$$

the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. The $n$-th ratio is therefore

$$R_{n}^{\star}
 =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M},
 \qquad R_{1}^{\star}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\star}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$. Numerically

$R_{1}^{\star}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\star}=3\cdot2^{-2}/[2(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\star}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\star}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\star}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

and $R_{n}^{\star}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. The series is super-exponentially convergent,

$$S_{\infty}^{\star}
  =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
  =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with the $n=1$ term equal to $1$ and the tail $<10^{-6}$ after $n=6$. This is the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-line cross-polytope normalisation.

The $1.117$ value obtained in Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 is the i.i.d. with-replacement version $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and the $1/n$ same-arm term $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ in $D_{n}$. That model keeps the $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability and hence allows a degenerate hull with positive probability, which is incompatible with the stated $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure and with the phrase “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” understood as a bijection. Under the intended distinct-arm reading the sum is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above, $ \approx1.250$ to three decimals.

4.text:
For the $n$-arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ let
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
Put $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.765195716 .
$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ so that with the
$1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}
   =(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, etc.

For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$,

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)} .
$

Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union, average-pair
normalisation

$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{0.375}{8/3+M_{0}}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}^{\rm iid}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}^{\rm iid}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$, $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

In particular

$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots $

and

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$

$R_{1}+R_{2}\approx1.1093$, $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}\approx1.117$,
the tail $n\ge4$ being $<5\times10^{-4}$.  The $n=1$ term is the
normalising $1$ and the whole $n\ge2$ remainder is $0.117\ldots$,
essentially the $n=2$ term $0.1093$.

Remark.  On the conventional one-point-per-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$, i.e.

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\bigl[n!\,\bigl(1+(n-1)M_{0}\bigr)\bigr]$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}
\approx0.03293$, etc., and

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the $1.250$ distinct-axis value usually quoted for the
one-point-per-orthogonal-line cross-polytope model.  This is the
$n!/n^{n}$ collision-free limit of the i.i.d. on-union calculation
above. ∎

3.text:
With the cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ put
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., 
$U_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
E_{2}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =0.7651957164\ldots
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so that with the
usual $1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|U|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{2}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)E_{2}}{n},
$$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}\,}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union, mean-over-all-pairs
normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}= \frac{1/16}{\,\bigl[1+D_{2}\bigr]/3\,}\approx0.10927,\qquad
R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\qquad
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\qquad
R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},
$$

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  In particular

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}+R_{2}
\approx1.1093$, $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}\approx1.117$.  The $n=1$ term is the
normalising $1$ and the whole $n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots$.

Remark.  On the conventional one-point-per-arm bijection
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$ one has $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)E_{2}]/(n+1)$ and

$$
R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)E_{2}]},
\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the $1.25$ distinct-axis value quoted in the literature.  The
$1.117$ above is the literal i.i.d. uniform-on-$\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$
reading of “an ensemble of independent stochastic points sampled on
the union”.

2.text:
The $d$ point set is
$S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$,
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Put $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
E_{2}:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   =M\approx0.765195716 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, so that
with the $1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E V_{d}:=E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{d}\right)
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|T|)^{d}}{d!}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{d}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}E_{2}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)M}{d},
$$

and for the $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2D_{d}}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)D_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}M\,}{d(d+1)} .
$$

Hence on the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average pair normalisation

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}M},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e.

$$
R_{d}= \frac{3d(d+1)}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}

* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,

   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots ,

$$
M:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots 
$$

On $\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}$,
$| \det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}Y_{i}$ and 
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so that with the

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(EY)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},\qquad
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, etc.

$$
D_{n}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M}{n},
$$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M}{n(n+1)} .
$$

$$

   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\frac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M}

$$

i.e.

$$

 =\frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}

$R_{2}= \dfrac{0.375}{8/3+M}\approx0.109271$,

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The cross is ${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ and the statement is “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual bijection one point per orthogonal arm, not $n$ i.i.d. draws from the union with replacement.

On the intended model

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}, \qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1) \ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

the simplex is a.s. non-degenerate, as an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure is required. Then

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{n}\right)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

so with $E|T|=1/2$

$$E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor that appears in the with-replacement calculation is absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$.  
With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$$

the mean pairwise distance in the realisation. Hence the conventional
normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M},
   \qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\sharp}= (n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$. Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/(4\times2(1+M))\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three figures, the $n=1$ term being $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$.

This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-line normalisation quoted by Colleagues 13,14,7 and noted as the “usual” normalisation in the remarks of Colleague 1,10,2. The $1.117$ value is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$, in which
$P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}>0$ is lost, the hull is degenerate with
probability $1-n!/n^{n}$, and $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$. That model allows
empty axes and a positive probability of a degenerate hull, in conflict
with the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” and
“the number of points and line segments matching the dimension”, which is
precisely the bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$. Under the intended distinct-arm
reading the sum is $1.250$ to three decimals.

   =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence on the average–pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   :=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

i.e.

$ R_{n}= \dfrac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
               {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}} $.

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=9/\!\left[8\bigl(8+3E_{0}\bigr)\right]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  The series is therefore essentially
exhausted by $n=1,2,3$,

$$
S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
       =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots,
$$

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
   =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
   \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002
   \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.109$,
$S_{3}\approx1.117$.  The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ i.i.d. on-the-union tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially the
$n=2$ term $0.1093$.

Remark.  With the usual one-point-per-orthogonal-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ a.s. distinct, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)E_{0}]/(n+1)$, so that

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\!\left[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)E_{0}\bigr)\right]$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx
0.03293$, etc., and $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,
the familiar distinct-axis value often quoted for the cross-polytope
model.  The $1.117$ above is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union,
$\binom{n+1}{2}$–average-pair normalisation described in the statement.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is the standard one-point-per-arm cross. 
The candidate set is ${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$,
$n$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin in the unit ball, and the problem says the number of points and the number of line segments match the dimension. That is the bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

On this model the hull is a.s. an $n$-simplex. With the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=
\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!}$,

$E|T|=1/2$, hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,

as usual for the random cross-polytope. The $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor
is absent because the axes are distinct by construction, which is
exactly what is needed for an a.s. $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}:=M$,

$M=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716$,

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,}$,

the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the
$n+1$ point set. Hence

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=
\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
 =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}$,

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$,

$R_{2}^{\sharp}= \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac1{1+M}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$, etc.

The series is super-exponential,

$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-line normalisation
quoted by Colleagues 13 and 14 and noted as the usual convention by
Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 12, 15, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9. The i.i.d. on-the-union
with-replacement reading $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\}$, gives $p_{n}=n!/n^{n}$ and $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$,
i.e. a degenerate hull with positive probability $1-n!/n^{n}$, and is the
non-standard $1.117$ average-pair artefact. With the distinct-arm
bijection implied by “number of points and line segments matching the
dimension” the intended sum is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above,
$\approx1.250$ to three decimals.

public_text.7:
The wording is the usual cross-polytope bijection and not an i.i.d. sample with replacement on the union.

Let ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ be the $n$-arm cross in the unit ball and let

$$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},$$

with $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. The statement “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” is the standard pairing one point per distinct mutually orthogonal open segment. In particular the hull is a.s. full dimensional, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, whereas an i.i.d. $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ makes the simplex degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and introduces the artificial $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor.

With the bijection model

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=2^{-n}/n! , \qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2.$$

For $i\ne j$ the two arms are orthogonal,

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =M:=\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$. With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $n+1$ points $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1}
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}M,$$

the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. The $n$-th ratio is therefore

$$R_{n}^{\star}
 =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M},
 \qquad R_{1}^{\star}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\star}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$. Numerically

$R_{1}^{\star}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\star}=3\cdot2^{-2}/[2(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\star}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\star}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\star}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

and $R_{n}^{\star}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. The series is super-exponentially convergent,

$$S_{\infty}^{\star}
  =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
  =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with the $n=1$ term equal to $1$ and the tail $<10^{-6}$ after $n=6$. This is the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-line cross-polytope normalisation.

The $1.117$ value obtained in Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 is the i.i.d. with-replacement version $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and the $1/n$ same-arm term $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ in $D_{n}$. That model keeps the $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability and hence allows a degenerate hull with positive probability, which is incompatible with the stated $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure and with the phrase “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” understood as a bijection. Under the intended distinct-arm reading the sum is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above, $ \approx1.250$ to three decimals.

For the $n$-arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ let

   \approx0.765195716 .
$

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}
   =(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, etc.

For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$,

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)} .
$

Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union, average-pair
normalisation

$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{0.375}{8/3+M_{0}}\approx0.10927$,

$R_{4}^{\rm iid}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}^{\rm iid}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$, $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

In particular

$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots $

and

 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots

For the $n$–arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ put
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,
$A_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., and
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  With $E|T|=1/2$,
$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   =0.765195716\ldots ,
\qquad S_{0}=3M_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),
$$

on $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{\,n}$, so that with the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$$
E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}
   =(2n)^{-n}, \qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, $\dots$

For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n},
$$
and for the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
  =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
  =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
  =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence on the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e.

$$
R_{n}= \frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}
\bigl[\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\bigl(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr)\bigr]}\; .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{1.125}{8/3+M_{0}}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$ and the tail is $<5\times10^{-4}$ for
$n\ge4$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}+R_{2}\approx
1.1093$, $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}\approx1.117$.  This is the i.i.d.
uniform-on-the-union $\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$ mean-over-all-pairs
normalisation, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$.

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\bigl[n!\,(1+(n-1)M_{0})\bigr]$, whence
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $1.25$

The cross is ${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ and the statement is “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual bijection one point per orthogonal arm, not $n$ i.i.d. draws from the union with replacement.

On the intended model

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}, \qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1) \ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

the simplex is a.s. non-degenerate, as an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure is required. Then

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{n}\right)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

so with $E|T|=1/2$

$$E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor that appears in the with-replacement calculation is absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$.  
With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$$

the mean pairwise distance in the realisation. Hence the conventional
normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M},
   \qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\sharp}= (n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$. Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/(4\times2(1+M))\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three figures, the $n=1$ term being $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$.

This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-line normalisation quoted by Colleagues 13,14,7 and noted as the “usual” normalisation in the remarks of Colleague 1,10,2. The $1.117$ value is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$, in which
$P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}>0$ is lost, the hull is degenerate with
probability $1-n!/n^{n}$, and $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$. That model allows
empty axes and a positive probability of a degenerate hull, in conflict
with the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” and
“the number of points and line segments matching the dimension”, which is
precisely the bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$. Under the intended distinct-arm
reading the sum is $1.250$ to three decimals.

E_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =0.765195716\ldots , 
\qquad S_{0}=3E_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2).
$$

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so with the usual
$1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}
   =(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, etc.
For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(n-1)E_{0}}{n},
$$

and for the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
   =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} .
$$

Hence on the average–pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   :=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}E_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

i.e.

$ R_{n}= \dfrac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
               {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}} $.

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=9/\!\left[8\bigl(8+3E_{0}\bigr)\right]\approx0.10927$,

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}

public_text.14:
The wording is the standard one-point-per-arm cross. 
The candidate set is ${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$,
$n$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin in the unit ball, and the problem says the number of points and the number of line segments match the dimension. That is the bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

On this model the hull is a.s. an $n$-simplex. With the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=
\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!}$,

$E|T|=1/2$, hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,

as usual for the random cross-polytope. The $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor
is absent because the axes are distinct by construction, which is
exactly what is needed for an a.s. $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}:=M$,

$M=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716$,

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,}$,

the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the
$n+1$ point set. Hence

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=
\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
 =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}$,

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$,

$R_{2}^{\sharp}= \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac1{1+M}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$, etc.

The series is super-exponential,

$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-line normalisation
quoted by Colleagues 13 and 14 and noted as the usual convention by
Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 12, 15, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9. The i.i.d. on-the-union
with-replacement reading $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\}$, gives $p_{n}=n!/n^{n}$ and $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$,
i.e. a degenerate hull with positive probability $1-n!/n^{n}$, and is the
non-standard $1.117$ average-pair artefact. With the distinct-arm
bijection implied by “number of points and line segments matching the
dimension” the intended sum is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above,
$\approx1.250$ to three decimals.
