4.text:
The $n$-arm cross

$${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n},
\qquad e_{k}\perp e_{\ell},\;k\ne \ell ,$$

is the usual model for a random cross-polytope.  The phrase
‘the number of points and the number of line segments matches the
dimension’ is the usual bijection one point per distinct orthogonal arm

$$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad 
X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},$$

so that $S_{n}$ is a.s. an $n$–simplex and an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue
measure is a.s. defined.  With the $1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor of the with-replacement model being
absent.  Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots ,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$.  For the
$N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,}$$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation.  Hence on the
conventional one-point-per-arm normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$$

i.e.

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,\;
R_{2}^{\sharp}= \frac{3}{4(1+M)}\approx0.21244,
\;R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293,
\;R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395,$$
and $R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ is super-exponentially convergent.
Summation gives

$$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.  This is the familiar
$2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis cross-polytope sum.

Remark.  On the literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots n\}$,
$P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n},\qquad 
D_{n}= \frac{2/3+(n-1)M}{n},\qquad
\bar D_{n}^{\rm iid}= \frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1},$$

so that

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $1.117$ average-pair i.i.d. value quoted in the remarks.  The
$1.250$ value above is the a.s. full-dimensional, one-point-per-orthogonal
arm, $n!/n^{n}$-free model implied by “number of points and line
segments matching the dimension’’ and by the requirement of an a.s.
$n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is the standard one-point-per-arm cross-polytope and not an i.i.d. with-replacement sampling on the union.

Let ${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}$ be the $n$-arm cross in the unit ball. The statement says the number of stochastic points and the number of distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments match the dimension. That is the bijection

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

one point on each distinct orthogonal arm. In particular the simplex is a.s. non-degenerate, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, whereas the with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ makes the hull degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and introduces the artificial $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor.

With the bijection

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the with-replacement calculation is absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$ the arms are orthogonal so $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$.
With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$$

the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the realised set.

Hence the conventional normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+M)}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three figures, the $n=1$ term being $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$.

This is the $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis value quoted by Colleagues 13,14,7 and noted as the usual normalisation in the remarks of Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9. The $1.117$ value is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$, in which the hull is degenerate with positive probability $1-n!/n^{n}$ and the $n^{-n}$ factor is a modelling artefact. Under the intended distinct-arm reading, “number of points and line segments matching the dimension”, the sum is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above, $\approx1.250$ to three decimals.

R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$
i.e. 
$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]} .
$$

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8\bigl(8+3M_{0}\bigr)]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Consequently

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$
to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$, $S_{3}\approx1.1168$, the tail
$n\ge4$ being $<5\times10^{-4}$.  The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ i.i.d. on–the–union tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one–point–per–orthogonal–arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ the collision factor $n!/n^{n}$ disappears,
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$
and
$$
R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]},
\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$
the familiar $1.25$ distinct–axis cross–polytope value quoted in
Colleagues 13,14,7.  The $1.117$ above is the literal i.i.d.
uniform–on–$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, $\binom{n+1}{2}$–average–pair
reading of “an ensemble of independent stochastic points sampled on the
union”. ∎

8.text:
On the $n$-arm cross

$${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n}, \qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

let the $n$ points be paired with the $n$ distinct orthogonal arms.  The
statement that the number of points and the number of distinct mutually
orthogonal open segments ``match the dimension’’ is the usual
one-point-per-arm bijection

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.}, $$

so that $S_{n}$ is a.s. a non-degenerate $n$-simplex.  With the $1/n!$
simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
        =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, $$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor of the with-replacement model being
absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.765195716, $$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$, $i\ne j$.  For the $N_{n}=
\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,},$$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation.  Hence the
conventional normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,\bigl[1+(n-1)M\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,
$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$.  Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.
This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-line cross-polytope normalisation.

*Remark.*  The literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., gives
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$D_{n}=n^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(n-1)n^{-1}M$,
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm iid}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$,

so that

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
       =\frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\bigl[5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}\bigr]},\qquad
S_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),$$

with $R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$ etc., and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ with-replacement average-pair value quoted in the
majority of the round-2 notes.  The $1.250$ value above is the
collision-free distinct-arm model intended by the “number of points and
line segments matching the dimension’’ formulation. ∎

9.text:
On the $n$-arm cross

${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n}$ let

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$
i.i.d., $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$,
$V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})$.  Put $E|T|=1/2$,
$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.765195716 ,
\qquad S_{0}=3M_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2) .
$$

${\mathbf P}\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$.  With the $1/n!$
simplex normalisation

$$
E V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

$EV_{1}=1/2$, $EV_{2}=1/16$, $EV_{3}=1/216$, $\dots$

For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n},
$$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} ,
$$

the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. Hence on the
$\binom{n+1}{2}$ average pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{EV_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

i.e.

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =\frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\Bigl[\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}
       \bigl(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr)\Bigr]} ,
$$

in particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Hence

$$
S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n\le N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
$$

and

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$
and $S_{3}\approx1.1168$.  The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ one has $EV_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$, whence

$$
R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]},
\qquad\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis value.  The $1.117$ above is the
literal i.i.d. uniform-on-${\cal C}_{n}$,
$\binom{n+1}{2}$-average-pair normalisation $EV_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ used in

The $n$-arm cross

$${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n},
\qquad e_{k}\perp e_{\ell},\;k\ne \ell ,$$

is the usual model for a random cross-polytope.  The phrase
‘the number of points and the number of line segments matches the
dimension’ is the usual bijection one point per distinct orthogonal arm

$$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad 
X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},$$

so that $S_{n}$ is a.s. an $n$–simplex and an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue
measure is a.s. defined.  With the $1/n!$ simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor of the with-replacement model being
absent.  Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots ,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$.  For the
$N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,}$$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation.  Hence on the
conventional one-point-per-arm normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$$

i.e.

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,\;
R_{2}^{\sharp}= \frac{3}{4(1+M)}\approx0.21244,
\;R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293,
\;R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395,$$
and $R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ is super-exponentially convergent.
Summation gives

$$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.  This is the familiar
$2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis cross-polytope sum.

Remark.  On the literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots n\}$,
$P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n},\qquad 
D_{n}= \frac{2/3+(n-1)M}{n},\qquad
\bar D_{n}^{\rm iid}= \frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1},$$

so that

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $1.117$ average-pair i.i.d. value quoted in the remarks.  The
$1.250$ value above is the a.s. full-dimensional, one-point-per-orthogonal
arm, $n!/n^{n}$-free model implied by “number of points and line
segments matching the dimension’’ and by the requirement of an a.s.
$n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. ∎

The wording is the standard one-point-per-arm cross-polytope and not an i.i.d. with-replacement sampling on the union.

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

one point on each distinct orthogonal arm. In particular the simplex is a.s. non-degenerate, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, whereas the with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ makes the hull degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and introduces the artificial $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor.

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E\,{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the with-replacement calculation is absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716,$$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$ the arms are orthogonal so $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$.

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 M}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$$

the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the realised set.

Hence the conventional normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.$$

$R_{2}^{\sharp}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+M)}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three figures, the $n=1$ term being $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$.

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so with the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},\qquad
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, … .

For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n},
$$
and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} ,
$$
the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the $n+1$
point set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

Hence on the $\binom{n+1}{2}$–average–pair normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$
i.e. 
$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]} .
$$

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8\bigl(8+3M_{0}\bigr)]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Consequently

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$
to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$, $S_{3}\approx1.1168$, the tail
$n\ge4$ being $<5\times10^{-4}$.  The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ i.i.d. on–the–union tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one–point–per–orthogonal–arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ the collision factor $n!/n^{n}$ disappears,
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$
and
$$
R_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]},
\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$
the familiar $1.25$ distinct–axis cross–polytope value quoted in
Colleagues 13,14,7.  The $1.117$ above is the literal i.i.d.
uniform–on–$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, $\binom{n+1}{2}$–average–pair
reading of “an ensemble of independent stochastic points sampled on the
union”. ∎

On the $n$-arm cross

$${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{i}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n}, \qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

let the $n$ points be paired with the $n$ distinct orthogonal arms.  The
statement that the number of points and the number of distinct mutually
orthogonal open segments ``match the dimension’’ is the usual
one-point-per-arm bijection

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.}, $$

so that $S_{n}$ is a.s. a non-degenerate $n$-simplex.  With the $1/n!$
simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
        =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$$

$E|T|=1/2$ and hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, $$

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor of the with-replacement model being
absent because the axes are distinct by construction.

Put

$$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.765195716, $$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$, $i\ne j$.  For the $N_{n}=
\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,},$$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation.  Hence the
conventional normalised ratio is

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,\bigl[1+(n-1)M\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,
$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M]\}$.  Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.
This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-line cross-polytope normalisation.

*Remark.*  The literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., gives
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$D_{n}=n^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(n-1)n^{-1}M$,
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm iid}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$,

so that

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
       =\frac{3n(n+1)}{(2n)^{n}\bigl[5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}\bigr]},\qquad
S_{0}=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),$$

with $R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$ etc., and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $n!/n^{n}$ with-replacement average-pair value quoted in the
majority of the round-2 notes.  The $1.250$ value above is the
collision-free distinct-arm model intended by the “number of points and
line segments matching the dimension’’ formulation. ∎

$|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and 
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$, so with the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
     = \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$ ,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$,

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,\;E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16,\;E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216,\dots $ .

For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$,

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the
$n+1$ point set.  Hence on the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average pair
normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   :=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]},
\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1 .
$$

In particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8\,(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

and

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$,
$S_{3}\approx1.117$.  The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one point per orthogonal arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ a.s. distinct, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$.  Then

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\bigl\{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]\bigr\}$,

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,\;R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244,\;R_{3}^{\sharp}
\approx0.03293$, etc., and

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]}
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis value.  This is the $n!/n^{n}$-free
limit of the i.i.d. on-the-union calculation above. ∎

i.i.d. uniform-on-union literal reading
* $X_i=T_i e_{A_i}$, $A_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$, $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
* $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_1-T_2|=2/3$, $M_0=E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}
 =\int_{0}^1\!\int_{0}^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765195716$.
* $p_n=n!/n^n$ distinct axes.
* $E{\rm Vol}_n =p_n (E|T|)^n/n!=(2n)^{-n}$ ; $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_2=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_3=1/216$.
* $D_n=E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(n-1)M_0]/n$.
* Mean unordered pair distance in $S_n=\{0,X_1..X_n\}$ :
$\bar D_n=[1+(n-1)D_n]/(n+1)=\bigl[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2M_0\bigr]/[n(n+1)]$.
* $R_n^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_n/\bar D_n
 =n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^2M_0]
 =(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_n]$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$.
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_n^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ to three decimals.
The $n=1$ term is $1$; tail beyond $n=4$ $<10^{-5}$.

* $X_i=T_i e_i$, $E{\rm Vol}_n^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$.
* $\bar D_n^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_0]/(n+1)$.

$R_1^{\sharp}=1$, $R_2^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The cross ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset{\mathbb B}^{n}$ is the usual $n$-arm cross. The statement that the number of points and the number of distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments ‘‘match the dimension’’ is the standard bijection reading: one random point on each arm. With

$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\;T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.,

the simplex is a.s. $n$-dimensional, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!}$,

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

The $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor that appears for an i.i.d. draw
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ is absent
because the axes are distinct by construction. The with-replacement model
makes the hull degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and therefore
has a positive probability of zero $n$-dimensional volume, which is
incompatible with the requirement of an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure
and with the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal’’.

Put

$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots $,

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$ because the arms
are orthogonal. With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$

the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. Hence the conventional
normalised ratio is

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
 =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Summation gives

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals. The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the remainder
is $0.2497$.

This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-arm, a.s. full-dimensional
$2^{-n}/n!$ cross-polytope normalisation. The $1.117$ figure quoted in the
remarks is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$, $P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}
=n!/n^{n}$, for which the hull is degenerate with positive probability and
the $n^{-n}$ factor is a modelling artefact. Under the intended distinct-arm
bijection implied by “number of points and line segments matching the
dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ the sum
is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above, $\approx1.250$ to three decimals.

4.text:
The $n$-arm cross is ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset
{\mathbb B}^{n}$ and on the literal independent-on-the-union reading

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\},
\qquad T_{i}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1), \qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots  $$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$. With the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, $\dots$
For $i\ne j$

$$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n},$$
and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)} $$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average–pair
normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\rm iid}=n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\big[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\big]$.
In particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$$

and

$$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$, $S_{3}\approx1.1168$.  The $n=1$
term is the normalising $1$ and the $n\ge2$ i.i.d. on-the-union tail is
$0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  With the conventional one-point-per-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ a.s. distinct, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$,
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$ and

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]},\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis, $n!/n^{n}$-free, a.s.
full-dimensional cross-polytope normalisation.  The $1.117$ above is the
literal i.i.d. uniform-on-$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$,
$\binom{n+1}{2}$-average-pair reading of an ensemble of independent
stochastic points on the union. ∎

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The phrasing is the standard cross-polytope bijection, not an i.i.d. with-replacement sample on the union.

${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset{\mathbb B}^{n}$ is $n$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin. “The number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and the requirement of an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of ${\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ means the hull is required to be a.s. $n$-dimensional. That is the usual one-point-per-arm model

$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\;T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.

With the $1/n!$ simplex normalisation

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|/n!=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|/n!$,

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor that only appears for a with-replacement i.i.d. draw $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ is absent because the axes are distinct by construction. In particular the hull is a.s. a non-degenerate $n$-simplex, as required for a genuine $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; the with-replacement model has ${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}<1$ and therefore a positive probability of a degenerate hull and zero $n$-volume.

For $i\ne j$ the arms are orthogonal so

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=M$,
$M=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots$,

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$. With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1}$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. The conventional normalised ratio is therefore

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Hence

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.

This is the $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis value noted as the usual convention in the remarks of Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15 and the primary value of Colleagues 13,14,7,4,8,10. The $1.117$ figure is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union average-pair calculation $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$, $D_{n}=[2/3+(n-1)M]/n$, $\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$, i.e. $R_{n}^{\rm iid}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$, which allows axis collisions and a positive probability of a degenerate hull. The problem statement’s “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ arms and “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is the a.s. full-dimensional bijection just described, giving the $1.250$ normalisation.

12.text:
On the $n$-arm cross
${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n}$ let

$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$, $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,
$A_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$T_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}U(-1,1)$,
so that the $n$ points are i.i.d. uniform on ${\cal C}_{n}$.
Put
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and
$$
M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With the $1/n!$ 
simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
 =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, etc.
For $i\ne j$

$$
D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
 =\frac{\,2/3+(n-1)M_{0}\,}{n},
$$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}
$$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average-pair
normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
 =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1 .
$$

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots ,
$$

and

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals on the literal
i.i.d. uniform-on-$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$,
$\binom{n+1}{2}$-average-pair reading.  The $n=1$ term is the
normalising $1$ and the $n\ge2$ tail is $0.117\ldots\approx R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  The collision-free one-point-per-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ a.s. distinct gives
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$ and
$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M_{0}]\}$,
with
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M_{0}]\}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,
the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis cross-polytope normalisation,
the $n!/n^{n}$-free limit of the calculation above. ∎

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$, $i\ne j$.  For the
$N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{\,n+1\,}$$

is the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation.  Hence on the
conventional one-point-per-arm normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}}{\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}}
   =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
   =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$$

i.e.

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\bigl\{n![1+(n-1)M]\bigr\}$.

Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. In
particular

$$S_{\infty}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250, $$

the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.  This is the a.s. full
dimensional, one-point-per-orthogonal-arm, $n!/n^{n}$-free
$2^{-n}/n!$ cross-polytope sum.

Remark. On the literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(n-1)M]/n$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm iid}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$.  Then

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
etc., and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the familiar $1.117$ with-replacement average-pair value.
The $1.250$ value above is the collision-free distinct-arm model
implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ and by the requirement of an
a.s. $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. ∎

3.text:
On the $n$-arm cross

$${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n},
\qquad S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\ldots ,X_{n}\}$$

put on the literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\},\;\;T_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}U(-1,1) , $$

so that $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots $$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$. With the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2, $$

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, etc.
For $i\ne j$

$$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}, $$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5n-2}{3}+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} ,$$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average-pair
normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

i.e.

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]} .$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=9/[8(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$. Hence

$$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots ,$$

and

$$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
   \approx1.1172,$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{2}\approx1.1093$,
$S_{3}\approx1.117$. The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ i.i.d. on-the-union tail is $0.117\ldots$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark. On the conventional a.s. full-dimensional one-point-per-arm
bijection $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$,
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$ and

$$R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]},\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M_{0}]}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis $1.25$ normalisation. This is the
$n!/n^{n}$-free $1.250$ limit of the i.i.d. on-the-union calculation
above. ∎

          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

i.e. 

$$

 =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
       {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]} .

public_text.7:
The cross ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset{\mathbb B}^{n}$ is the usual $n$-arm cross. The statement that the number of points and the number of distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments ‘‘match the dimension’’ is the standard bijection reading: one random point on each arm. With

$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\;T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.,

the simplex is a.s. $n$-dimensional, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!}$,

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

The $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor that appears for an i.i.d. draw
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ is absent
because the axes are distinct by construction. The with-replacement model
makes the hull degenerate with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$ and therefore
has a positive probability of zero $n$-dimensional volume, which is
incompatible with the requirement of an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure
and with the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal’’.

Put

$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots $,

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$ because the arms
are orthogonal. With $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$

the mean unordered pair distance in the realisation. Hence the conventional
normalised ratio is

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
 =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Summation gives

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals. The $n=1$ term is the normalising $1$ and the remainder
is $0.2497$.

This is the one-point-per-orthogonal-arm, a.s. full-dimensional
$2^{-n}/n!$ cross-polytope normalisation. The $1.117$ figure quoted in the
remarks is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$, $P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}
=n!/n^{n}$, for which the hull is degenerate with positive probability and
the $n^{-n}$ factor is a modelling artefact. Under the intended distinct-arm
bijection implied by “number of points and line segments matching the
dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ the sum
is the $2^{-n}/n!$ series above, $\approx1.250$ to three decimals.

The $n$-arm cross is ${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\},
\qquad T_{i}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1), \qquad 
S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},$$

$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots  $$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$. With the $1/n!$ simplex
normalisation

$$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, $\dots$
For $i\ne j$

$$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n},$$
and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)} $$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average–pair
normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{n}^{\rm iid}=n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\big[(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}\big]$.

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=9/[8(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$$

$$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
 \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

The cross

${\cal C}_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb B}^{n}$ 

is $n$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin. The statement that the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments “match the dimension’’ is the usual bijection reading: one random point on each arm. With

$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\},\qquad X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i},\;T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},$

the set is a.s. an $n$-simplex, as required for an $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In particular the hull is a.s. full dimensional, whereas the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
has $P\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}<1$ and a degenerate hull with probability $1-n!/n^{n}>0$. The $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor is therefore an artefact of a with-replacement sampling and is incompatible with the requirement of an a.s. $n$-dimensional volume.

With the bijection

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}S_{n})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|}{n!},$

$E|T|=1/2$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!,\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2.$

Put

$M=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots,$

$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=M$ for $i\ne j$ because the arms are orthogonal. For the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}= \frac{n\frac12+\binom n2M}{N_{n}}
  =\frac{1+(n-1)M}{n+1},$

the mean unordered pair distance of the realisation. Hence the conventional normalised ratio is

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}/\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)M}
 =\frac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)M]},\qquad R_{1}^{\sharp}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\sharp}=3/[4(1+M)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\sharp}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\sharp}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{\sharp}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$ super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}(n+1)}{n![1+(n-1)M]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the normalising $1$.

This is the $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-arm, $n!/n^{n}$-free normalisation that is the a.s. full-dimensional model implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ and “the number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’. The $1.117$ value repeatedly quoted in the remarks is the with-replacement i.i.d. on-the-union variant $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ with $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$, $D_{n}=[2/3+(n-1)M]/n$ and $\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$, i.e. $R_{n}^{\rm iid}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$ and $\sum_{n}R_{n}^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172$. It allows empty axes and a positive probability of a degenerate hull and is the usual $n!/n^{n}$ artefact noted as a remark in the i.i.d. derivations. Under the intended one-point-per-orthogonal-arm bijection the sum is the $1.250$ series above.

$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots $ .

=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and ${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n},

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$, $\dots$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$,

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)}$

union reading

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\},\;T_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}U(-1,1)$ , 
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$M_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots $

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}{\rm\;distinct}\}$
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|=\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbf P}\{A_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With the $1/n!$
simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_{2}=1/16$, $E{\rm Vol}_{3}=1/216$,
etc.

For $i\ne j$

$D_{n}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac1nE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}M_{0}
     =\frac{2/3+(n-1)M_{0}}{n}$

and with $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE\|X\|+\binom n2D_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}{n(n+1)}$

is the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

Hence on the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ average-pair normalisation

$R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{(5n-2)/3+(n-1)^{2}M_{0}}
   =\frac{3n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {5n-2+(n-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]}$,
$R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1$,

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}=9/[8\,(8+3M_{0})]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}^{\rm iid}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.
In particular

$S_{N}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{n\le N}R_{n}^{\rm iid}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

and

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002\ldots
   \approx1.1172,$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=1.117$ to three decimals.  The $n=1$ term is
the normalising $1$ and the $n\ge2$ i.i.d. on-the-union tail is
$0.117\ldots\approx R_{2}+R_{3}$.
This is the literal independent-points uniform-on-$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$
$\binom{n+1}{2}$ average-pair value.

Remark.  On the conventional one-point-per-orthogonal-arm bijection
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{i}$ a.s. distinct, the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor
disappears, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\sharp}=[1+(n-1)M_{0}]/(n+1)$ and

$R_{n}^{\sharp}=2^{-n}(n+1)/\{n![1+(n-1)M_{0}]\}$,
$R_{1}^{\sharp}=1$, $R_{2}^{\sharp}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\sharp}
\approx0.03293$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis cross-polytope normalisation
quoted as the a.s. full-dimensional $n!/n^{n}$-free limit. ∎
